macro.headline: Indices holding uptrend, but momentum fading and rotation broadening
macro.story:
The tape reads mixed under the hood. SPY sits at 745.76, up 1.7% over five sessions and 8.4% above its 200-day, but the daily MACD histogram is negative (-0.50) and the index gave back 0.14% Wednesday. QQQ mirrors this — up 2.1% on the week yet MACD-bearish and off 2.3% over 21 days. The Dow (RSI 65) and Russell 2000 (RSI 62) are actually the strongest indices, both with positive MACD, hinting at rotation away from mega-cap tech into cyclicals and small caps. VIX is 16.5, down 12.7% in five days, and the Engine C washout state reads CALM (SPY RSI 54.9, above 200-day) — no timing signal engaged. Commodities are broken: WTI crude -6.7% on the week and -28.4% on the month with RSI 27, gold -9.2% on 21 days, silver -20%. DXY is firm at 101.2 (RSI 64), and the 10Y-2Y spread has collapsed 30% in five days to just 0.23bp.

The tracked sentiment offers a coherent explanation for the split personality. The dominant view leans bullish on the AI capex theme — the conversation is heavy on META extending sharply on cloud-infrastructure reports, plus chatter around GOOGL, ORCL, and AI-adjacent names, framing this as institutional concentration into the compute stack rather than broad risk-on. At the same time, the tracked conversation is flagging a soft June payrolls print (57k versus 114k expected) as evidence of slowing labor demand, alongside a chart read showing retail participation in Mag7 hitting a four-year low. A smaller bearish lean is calling out QQQ and SPY specifically. This aligns with the price data: mega-cap tech leadership is narrowing (Nasdaq 100 sector score just 5.8, MACD bearish) while breadth-driven Financials, Healthcare, and Industrials do the heavy lifting. The oil collapse is not directly attributed in today's pulse, though the active themes list points to Iran/Hormuz de-escalation and rising US crude production as structural drivers — labeled as theme context, not live sentiment.

Sector-wise, the leadership board reads clean: Financials (score 10, RSI 68.5, bullish MACD cross), Healthcare (9.8), and Industrials (9.2) are all HOT, and the Russell 2000 is HOT alongside them. Technology has slipped to NEUTRAL/WEAK (score 4.8, MACD bearish), and Energy is outright broken (score 1.8, RSI 33.2). Rotation Radar validates this — Early-Runway industries fire in Travel Services, Diagnostics & Research, Credit Services, Staffing, and Drug Manufacturers, with rotation scores 0.87–0.97. These are the validated hunting grounds.

Forward watch: the flattening 10Y-2Y (down 51% on 21 days) alongside a DXY rally and collapsing crude is the classic late-cycle cocktail — worth respecting even as equity breadth holds. If Financials/Industrials/Healthcare keep leading and small caps confirm, the rotation is healthy. If MACD on SPY/QQQ stays negative into next week and Tech deteriorates further, the top-line index calm masks a real regime shift.
